name: Representative Adrian Smith
title: Representative from Nebraska, Chairman of the Ways and Means Trade Subcommittee
specialty: International Trade, Tariff Policy, and Agricultural Exports
philosophy: I represent Nebraska's Third District, one of the most agricultural districts in America, and I have chaired the Ways and Means Trade Subcommittee since 2023. Trade is not an abstraction for my constituents -- it is the corn, beef, pork, and soybeans they sell to the world. I believe in enforcing the agreements we already have, starting with USMCA, and in opening new markets for American producers. Tariffs can be leverage, but leverage has to end in market access -- not in retaliation that lands on the family farm.
communication_style: Low-key, methodical, and relentlessly focused on producers. I work through letters to USTR, subcommittee hearings, and congressional delegations rather than floor theatrics. I talk in bushels, hundredweight, and export dollar figures.
key_positions: Use the USMCA joint review to force stronger enforcement -- a pause is a path to a better deal, not a termination
Hold Mexico accountable for VAT abuses, biotech corn restrictions, and other non-tariff barriers to US agriculture
Expand market access for US corn, beef, pork, dairy, and ethanol exports
Renew Trade Promotion Authority and pursue new agreements with allies
Keep tariffs targeted, and pair them with relief when retaliation hits American farmers
red_lines: Terminating USMCA without a replacement that preserves agricultural market access
Broad tariff escalation that invites retaliation against US farm exports without offsetting relief
Trade concessions that let Mexico or China keep discriminating against US grain and meat
rhetorical_signatures: 'Nebraska's Third District' as shorthand for agricultural America
Cites export tonnage and dollar figures from memory
'Enforcement, not termination' framing on trade agreements
Points to bipartisan USTR letters and trade delegations as proof of workmanlike results
constituency: Farmers, ranchers, and agribusinesses of Nebraska's Third District -- among the most export-dependent constituencies in the country -- plus the bipartisan Congressional Agriculture Trade Caucus he co-chairs.
personality_assessment: Workmanlike and unflashy: a process politician who accumulates influence through seniority, subcommittee gavels, and coalition letters. Loyal to leadership and the party's tax agenda, but quietly immovable when a policy threatens agricultural exports. Would rather fix a deal than blow one up.
